title: Rehab for a child with cerebral palsy
also: rehabilitation for a child with cerebral palsy
what: These are regular sessions that help a child move, sit, walk, and care for themselves better. Doctors, instructors, and parents all take part.
why: For children with cerebral palsy, from an early age and throughout growth.
duration: a session usually takes 30 to 60 minutes, and courses are repeated many times
tell_doctor: What your child can do now and what has changed
Which medicines and injections your child gets
Whether they wear braces or use a wheelchair or walker
What your child and you want to learn to do

prepare.title: Goals
prepare.text: Think about what matters most to your child now: sitting, walking, holding a spoon. Tell the specialist.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes in which movements can be seen. Bring braces and shoes.

prepare.title: Routine
prepare.text: Plan the session for when your child is rested and not hungry.

steps: The specialist meets your child and watches how they move
Together with you, goals are set for the coming months
Braces, supports, and mobility aids are chosen
You are shown what to do with your child at home
feel: Your child may get tired or fussy, which is normal
Muscle stretching can be unpleasant, and the specialist adjusts the force
after: Practice at home every day, which is just as important as the sessions at the center
Wear braces on the schedule you were given
Praise your child for every new skill
red_flags: A seizure lasting more than 5 minutes, or your child does not come round: call emergency services
Sudden joint pain, or your child stopped putting weight on a leg

faq.a: It does not go away completely. But sessions help a child become more independent.

faq.q: How long do we need to practice?
faq.a: Regularly and for a long time, for years. A little every day is better than a lot rarely.

reminders.text: Your child's session is today. Bring braces, shoes, water, and a favorite toy.
